title: Earlier temperature windows gave no median gain for Japan cherry dates at a 38-day median lead in 2005-2024
abstract: We tested whether earlier temperature windows or past-mean weather fills recover advance skill for Japanese cherry dates. We fitted 115 station-phase series at 58 stations through 2004 and tested 2005-2024. Each issue month was fixed from training dates. With observed weather, median skill against a five-year trailing mean was 0.490. Two months before reference month-end, all 2,268 events were still in the future, with a median lead of 38 days. Refitted earlier windows gave median skill -0.024 (station-bootstrap 95% interval -0.094 to 0.027); the paired loss from the observed-weather fit was -0.522. Filling unknown weather from past monthly means gave zero median gain. One-month-early refits retained skill of 0.434, but 25.7% of events had already occurred. Results at the early deadlines stayed near zero with ten-year histories and in both test decades. This extends a prior availability audit by fitting new models and measuring actual event leads. Limits: one previously tested family, revised archives, monthly temperature only, no reporting lag, no archived weather forecasts or process models.

display.caption: Median forward skill and actual issue-to-event days for fixed training-based deadlines. Bars show station-bootstrap intervals.
